findings.claim: A Loro peer cannot apply entities it first learns from another peer because incoming snapshots are read only for IDs already present in the local `seenIds` set.
findings.evidence: The hunk initializes `seenIds.set(type, new Set<EntityId>())` when a doc is created, only adds IDs in `pushLocalChange` via `ids.add(id)`, and `handleIncomingBytes` imports peer bytes without adding any entity IDs from the imported document before the code path documented as `Read all entities from a doc given the set of known ids`; this breaks the claimed WebSocket/loopback first-sync convergence where a receiver has not locally seen the entity ID.
findings.suggested_fix: After `doc.import(bytes)`, derive entity IDs from the imported Loro document/root map (for example from `doc.toJSON().entities` or a map key iterator) and merge them into `seenIds` before building peer changes, or stop using a separate `seenIds` filter and enumerate the document contents directly.
